root_cause: Console._write_buffer runs after every print. When record=True it appended the whole of self._buffer to _record_buffer on each call, but during capture() (_buffer_index > 0) the buffer is never flushed or cleared. Each print inside a capture therefore re-recorded everything captured so far (Print1, Print1 Print2, ...). Captured output, which never reaches the terminal, was also being recorded.
best_solution: In Console._write_buffer, change `if self.record:` to `if self.record and not self._buffer_index:`. Output is then recorded only when the buffer is really flushed to the file (buffer index 0). That removes the repeated appends, and captured-only output stays out of the recording, so export_text() holds exactly what went to the terminal. The reasoning: work out when _write_buffer fires (after every print, through _exit_buffer and _check_buffer) and when the buffer is cleared (only at index 0, or in end_capture). Recording must be tied to the flush, not to each call.
acceptable_alternatives: Any change that records only the segments actually written to the output file, e.g. moving the record-extend inside the `if self._buffer_index == 0:` branch just before the write. A fix that only dedupes (records each captured segment once) still FAILS, because the test requires captured content to be excluded from the recording entirely.

our_outcome_summary:
All four configs failed (kaggle_env_pass v4/v6/v7/v8 = false). v4 (74s, 55 calls) and v6 (126s, 101 calls) submitted only new repro scripts (reproduce_issue.py, repro_fix.py) with no source change. v6's repro even asserted the wrong semantics (captured text recorded). v7 (94s, 44 calls) produced an empty patch. v8 (150s, 54 calls) edited the wrong place: it loosened the `assert self.record` guard in export_text/export_html to `self.record or self._record_buffer`, which leaves the duplication untouched. The p_v4 log shows the base behavior: export_text returned 'Print 0
Print 1
Print 1
Print 2
...' against the expected 'Print 0
'. No config touched _write_buffer.
generalizable_lesson: When the statement is only a PR title like 'Fix X and Y' (two features interacting), first write a small repro that exercises both together several times in a row (not once). Then trace every call site that feeds the shared state, here the append into a record buffer, and check whether it is guarded by the same condition that flushes or clears the source buffer. Accumulate-without-clear bugs show up only on the 2nd+ call. When picking semantics, prefer 'the recording mirrors what was actually emitted' and tie the side effect to the real flush point. An existing test encoding the old behavior may be replaced by the hidden test, so don't treat it as the spec. Never submit a patch that only adds repro scripts: a source change is required.
